rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2, 4.1 - authors built an IoT weather station and embedded prototype at tomato greenhouses in Tulancingo, Hidalgo, Mexico, recorded five climatic variables every 10 min for 365 days and fitted ANN/regression models; they also designed a fuzzy sprinkler controller (Section 4.3, Tables 11-12, Figs 12-13). Q2: Section 4.1-4.2, Fig 9 (comparative graphs of measured data vs ANN model for summer and winter), Table 6 and Sections 4.2.1-4.2.13 - monthly and annual models of inside temperature from outside climate variables, with R2 from about 80% to 96.6% and annual adjusted R2 95.79%, checked against measured inside temperature; Section 4.3, Tables 11-12, Figs 12-13 - fuzzy associative memory maps predicted and cropland temperature to 0-100% PWM pump activation in five frost classes. Q8: Conclusions - the method needs extensive data (every 10 min for 365 days) to reach R2 above 95%, and the annual model shows an indication of serial correlation of residuals (DW P < 0.05); Section 3.1.1 - ANN is a black box whose validity depends only on performance, difficult to interpret and can be over-trained. Q9: Table 8 - standard errors of all regression coefficients per month; Table 1 - standard error and 95% lower/upper confidence limits for ROC area; Table 6 - standard error of estimate per month.
rows.notes: The study's own data support only the prediction half of the passage: ANN predictions of inside greenhouse temperature are compared with measurements. The fuzzy anti-frost controller is designed and its rule base/PWM outputs are reported (Tables 11-12), but no measurement of the resulting frost protection or microclimate change (e.g. inside temperature with vs without sprinkling, crop damage avoided) is reported; the ice-sheet insulation mechanism is asserted in the Introduction, not measured. Single site, one crop (tomato), greenhouse scale only. Q9 is a borderline yes: the dispersion measures (coefficient SEs, ROC 95% CL) relate to the model fit; the residual standard error alone would be a validation error. Q7 set to no because the only stated requirement (need for very frequent, year-long data) is framed as a disadvantage of achieving high R2 rather than a condition for frost control.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2 and 4 - own IoT weather station, year-long 10-min climatic data, ANN/regression models of greenhouse inside temperature and a fuzzy sprinkler controller at tomato greenhouses in Hidalgo, Mexico.
rows.notes: The study reports no result on water use, water saving or irrigation scheduling efficiency. Its sprinkler system sprays water on the greenhouse plastic cover to form an insulating ice layer during frost; it is not crop irrigation and no water volumes or water-use outcomes are measured. What the study actually shows is ANN prediction accuracy for inside greenhouse temperature (monthly R2 80-97%, annual adjusted R2 95.8%, Fig 9, Table 6) and the design of a fuzzy rule base/FAM for PWM pump activation under five frost classes (Tables 11-12). The ML-in-predictive-modeling part of the passage is reflected in the study, but the claimed effect (efficient smart irrigation / water conservation) is not evidenced.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a single-site engineering/prototype study: validated ANN temperature prediction, but the anti-frost irrigation effect itself is designed and described, never measured. Figures are referenced but not visible; ratings rely on text and tables.
